summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery bypass grafting, aortic valve replacement, and prior stroke presented with hypotension and lightheadedness after a recent episode of hypertensive emergency and seizures. She had undergone aggressive fluid removal during dialysis, leading to volume depletion and relative hypotension. Her troponin was mildly elevated, consistent with demand ischemia from prior stressors. An echocardiogram showed a well-functioning bioprosthetic aortic valve and hyperdynamic left ventricular function without acute changes. Clonidine was reduced, IV fluids were given, and lisinopril was not restarted. She stabilized, tolerated dialysis without fluid removal, and was discharged home with updated medications and follow-up plans.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Heart valve replaced by other means
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
